text: broken and stuttering. Jake clung white-knuckled to the edge of the trapdoor above, staring down through sweat-stung eyes, waiting to see if they’d actually done it in time. Dwight coughed, deep and painful, spots flashing in his vision. He blinked slowly, voice shredded. “...I think I hate that guy.” Bill snorted, half relief, half disbelief, trying not to wince at the bruise blooming under his spine. “Yeah, well... get in line.” Jake barked out a laugh then, sharp and a little wild, spilling loose from where he dangled over the edge. Relief, hysteria—it didn’t matter. The sound broke the tension like a snapped rope, echoing across the gallows. A whistle floated through the mist. Low. Casual. Caleb was still out there. The chain lay coiled in the dirt beside them, the mark of a moment survived—but not escaped.
